name: NAPRUTI lactobacilli
question: Are oral Lactobacillus rhamnosus GR-1 and Lactobacillus reuteri RC-14 noninferior to daily trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for preventing recurrent UTI in postmenopausal women?

arms.label: Oral Lactobacillus rhamnosus GR-1 and Lactobacillus reuteri RC-14 twice daily

design.population: 252 community-dwelling postmenopausal women with at least three self-reported symptomatic UTIs in the preceding year, recruited through Dutch advertisements and clinicians at 10 centers.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, double-dummy noninferiority randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods, p 705; Table 1 and Figure 1, pp 705, 707

verdictNote: Noninferiority failed; TMP-SMX delayed recurrence but increased E. coli resistance.
takeaway: In postmenopausal women, oral L. rhamnosus GR-1 plus L. reuteri RC-14 failed noninferiority to daily trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for symptomatic UTI prevention: 3.3 versus 2.9 recurrences over 12 months (difference 0.4, 95% CI −0.4 to 1.5). TMP-SMX increased E. coli resistance.

reports.label: 12-month randomized report
reports.citation: Beerepoot MAJ, ter Riet G, Nys S, et al. "Lactobacilli vs Antibiotics to Prevent Urinary Tract Infections: A Randomized, Double-blind, Noninferiority Trial in Postmenopausal Women." *Arch Intern Med.* 2012;172(9):704-712. doi:10.1001/archinternmed.2012.777
reports.followUp: 12 months of prophylaxis plus 3 months after discontinuation
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods, pp 705–706; Table 2, p 708

results.measure: Mean clinical recurrences over 12 months; mean difference, lactobacilli minus TMP-SMX
results.note: The prespecified 10% noninferiority margin was exceeded: relative difference 13.8% (95% CI −13.8% to 51.7%). The paper defines ITT as participants who took at least one dose.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 706–707; Results, p 707; Table 2, p 708

results.measure: Kaplan-Meier estimated proportion during 12 months of prophylaxis
results.note: Primary clinical outcome without a separate prespecified success threshold; percentages are Kaplan–Meier estimates, not simple n/N fractions.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 706; Table 2, p 708

results.note: Primary clinical outcome without a separate prespecified success threshold; P value is from the log-rank test.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 707; Table 2 and Figure 2B, p 708

results.measure: Mean recurrences over 12 months; mean difference, lactobacilli minus TMP-SMX
results.note: Microbiologic recurrence required symptoms and at least 10^3 CFU/mL in midstream urine; no prespecified success threshold.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 706; Results, p 707; Table 2, p 708

results.endpoint: Symptomatic UTI recurrence by complicated UTI status
results.measure: Mean clinical recurrences over 12 months, prespecified subgroup analysis
results.note: Prespecified subgroup analysis; no subgroup denominators or confirmatory success threshold reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 706; Results, pp 707–708

results.measure: Percentage of TMP-SMX-resistant E. coli isolates from feces and asymptomatic urine at months 1 and 12; other antibiotic resistance assessed

values.ctl: Approximately 20%-40% at baseline to 80%-95% after one month

results.note: Primary resistance outcome without a prespecified success threshold. Isolate denominators varied by sample and time (fecal 56–99; urinary 30–53); all asymptomatic urinary E. coli isolates after 12 months of TMP-SMX were resistant to TMP-SMX and trimethoprim.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 706; Results, p 707; Figure 3 and caption, pp 709–710

harms.label: Any adverse event
harms.note: Among women in the treatment analysis population.

harms.label: Serious adverse event
harms.note: One systemic allergic reaction in the TMP-SMX arm was judged likely treatment-related.

harms.label: Adverse event leading to withdrawal
harms.note: A masked safety board judged treatment association likely for 11/123 (8.9%) versus 3/115 (2.6%).

harms.label: UTI requiring hospitalization
harms.note: Classified as unlikely to be treatment-related.

harms.label: Nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea
harms.note: Adverse-event category; no significant difference reported for adverse events overall.

delivery.label: Double-dummy prophylaxis
delivery.value: For 12 months, lactobacilli recipients took a capsule containing at least 10^9 CFU of the two-strain preparation twice daily plus a nightly placebo tablet; TMP-SMX recipients took 480 mg nightly plus twice-daily placebo capsules.

delivery.label: Treatment analysis set
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods (Statistical Analysis), p 706; Figure 1, p 707
delivery.note: The article calls this intention-to-treat and includes women who took at least one study dose.

delivery.label: Vaginal microbiology
delivery.value: L. reuteri was not detected in vaginal swabs in either arm at baseline or month 12; month-12 mean Nugent scores were 6.0 with lactobacilli and 6.1 with TMP-SMX.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results (Changes in Vaginal Microflora), p 708

delivery.label: Month-12 follow-up
delivery.note: Participants with follow-up at month 12 among those who received assigned treatment; not an adherence measure.

relations.note: Interlinked NAPRUTI trials tested nonantibiotic prophylaxis against TMP-SMX in different menopausal populations and with different agents.
